章节.Stations served by all trains:
As of 2023, the stations served by all regular passenger trains on the Sanyo Shinkansen are described below. All of them are stations in cities designated by government ordinance.

Of these, Shin-Osaka Station, Okayama Station, Hiroshima Station, Kokura Station, and Hakata Station have been stations served by all trains since the opening. Shin-Kobe Station initially had passing trains scheduled, but became a station served by all trains with the timetable revision of October 1, 2003.
章节.Shin-Osaka Station:
Located in the northern part of Osaka City, it was established in 1964 (Showa 39) at the opening of the Tokaido Shinkansen as the terminus of that line, at the crossing position with the Tokaido Main Line. From 1972 (Showa 47) it became the starting station of the Sanyo Shinkansen, and with the privatization and division of JNR in 1987 (Showa 62) it became a station shared with the Central Japan Railway Company (JR Central). At this station, trains of both the Tokaido and Sanyo Shinkansen each turn back, and through trains are also operated, so it has a large premises with five platforms and eight tracks.
In addition to the Tokaido Main Line (JR Kyoto Line) and the Osaka Higashi Line, it connects with the Osaka Metro Midosuji Line, linking the central part of Osaka City and the eastern and northern parts of Osaka Prefecture. On the other hand, since opening, limited express trains to the Hokuriku and Sanin regions have arrived at and departed from the station as long-distance conventional trains, and from 1989 (Heisei 1) limited express trains to the Wakayama and Nanki regions also began entering the station; furthermore, in 1994 (Heisei 6), with the opening of Kansai International Airport, the limited express "Haruka" to that airport was introduced, providing connections with the Shinkansen to all directions.
章节.Shin-Kobe Station:
The city of Kobe forms a long, narrow urban area from east to west, sandwiched between Mount Rokko to the north and Osaka Bay to the south. The Sanyo Shinkansen avoids the urban area and passes through the city by means of two long tunnels, the Rokko Tunnel and the Kobe Tunnel, and this station is located in the gap between these two tunnels. Due to topographical constraints, passing lines and refuge lines cannot be provided, and opposed side platforms are installed directly on the up and down main lines. In addition, because trains passing through this station were scheduled until September 30, 2003, platform doors have been installed since the opening.
For these reasons, this station has become a Shinkansen-only station about 1 km away from the conventional lines, with no direct connection to other JR lines, but it connects with the Kobe Municipal Subway, and through the Seishin-Yamate Line toward the Kobe city center, opened in 1985 (Showa 60), it connects with JR conventional lines at stations such as Sannomiya. To the northern part of Kobe City, it provides access via the Hokushin Line, connecting with Kobe Electric Railway at Tanigami Station and also to Sanda and Arima Onsen. On the other hand, this station is designated as a station within Kobe City under the specific metropolitan area system, and transfers to JR conventional lines via other companies' lines such as the subway are exceptionally permitted. In addition, JR Bus group highway buses to Tokushima and Awaji Island also have services arriving at and departing from this station.
章节.Okayama Station:
Located in Kita Ward, Okayama City, it opened in 1891 (Meiji 24) as a station of the Sanyo Railway (later the Sanyo Main Line). Entry of the Sanyo Shinkansen began in 1972 (Showa 47). It is also the starting station of the Kibi Line, the Tsuyama Line, and the Uno Line, and including the Ako Line and Hakubi Line, which branch from nearby stations, it forms a major route network in the surrounding area.
It is also positioned as a hub of wide-area transport, functioning as the gateway to Shikoku via the Uno Line and the Seto Ohashi Line. Initially it connected to Takamatsu Station via the Uno-Takamatsu Ferry, but since the opening of the Seto Ohashi Bridge in 1988 (Showa 63), limited express and rapid trains connecting this station with all parts of Shikoku via the bridge have been operated. In addition, with the opening of the Shinkansen, limited express trains connecting the Sanin region, such as Yonago and Matsue, via the Hakubi Line began operating. Connections with the Shinkansen have been arranged for all of these, and the station functions as a hub station for the Chugoku and Shikoku regions, not just the surrounding area. Between the tentative opening of Okayama in 1972 and the opening of Hakata in 1975 (Showa 50), limited express and express trains to Kyushu departing from this station were also scheduled.
章节.Hiroshima Station: Located in Minami Ward, Hiroshima City, it is the station with the largest number of passengers in the Chugoku and Shikoku regions. It opened in 1894 (Meiji 27) with the extension of the Sanyo Railway. The Sanyo Shinkansen began entering the station in 1975 (Showa 50) at the time of the full-line opening. It is the terminus of the Geibi Line, and trains on the Kure Line and Kabe Line also arrive and depart via the Sanyo Main Line. In addition, four lines of the Hiroshima Electric Railway (city trains) enter the station, extending their routes into the surrounding area. At the south exit there is a bus terminal, with city and suburban buses of Hiroden Bus, Hiroshima Bus, Hiroshima Kotsu, and others arriving and departing; it forms, together with the Hiroshima Bus Center, the two great bus terminals of Hiroshima City, and redevelopment continues there as of 2023. From the Shinkansen exit, highway buses mainly of JR Bus to the Sanin region (Matsue, Izumo, Hamada, Yonago, Masuda) and to Takamatsu arrive and depart, and although somewhat smaller in scale than Okayama Station, it functions as a hub of wide-area transport to the Chugoku and Shikoku regions.
章节.Kokura Station:
Located in Kokurakita Ward, Kitakyushu City, it is the representative station of that city and is also positioned as the gateway to Kyushu on the Sanyo Shinkansen. Kitakyushu City was born in 1963 (Showa 38) through the merger of five cities including Kokura City, and the station name has continued to be used as the name of the region without being changed.
It opened in 1891 (Meiji 24) as a station of the Kyushu Railway. It was later nationalized, and entry of the Sanyo Shinkansen began in 1975 (Showa 50). With the privatization and division of JNR in 1987 (Showa 62), jurisdiction, like neighboring Hakata Station, was divided: "the Shinkansen to JR West and the conventional lines to the Kyushu Railway Company (JR Kyushu)". It is the junction of the Kagoshima Main Line and the Nippo Main Line, two major trunk lines in Kyushu, and functions as a transfer station with limited express trains on the Nippo Main Line heading for the Oita region. In addition, the Kokura Line of the Kitakyushu Urban Monorail extends from in front of the station.
章节.Hakata Station:
The representative station of Fukuoka City. Like Kokura Station, it uses the name of the region rather than the name of the city. It opened in 1889 (Meiji 22) as a station of the Kyushu Railway and was nationalized in 1907 (Meiji 40). In 1975 (Showa 50) it became the terminus of the Sanyo Shinkansen, with limited express conventional trains connecting the cities of Kyushu such as Kagoshima, Kumamoto, Nagasaki, Sasebo, and Oita arriving and departing, and it became a transfer station with those trains and the Shinkansen. It also connects with the Fukuoka City Subway, and provides access to Fukuoka Airport to the east of the station, to Tenjin, the most prosperous entertainment district in Kyushu, and further to Karatsu via the Chikuhi Line. The Fukuhoku Yutaka Line to the Chikuho region also arrives and departs. In addition, a connecting line extends to the Hakata General Rolling Stock Depot, and this is used for sectional trains on the Hakata-Minami Line, a conventional line, as far as Hakata-Minami Station.
On March 12, 2011 (Heisei 23), the Kyushu Shinkansen (Kagoshima route) was extended to this station and fully opened. Through operation is also carried out as the Sanyo-Kyushu Shinkansen system. In line with the opening, expansion work was carried out within the station premises, which became a layout of three platforms and six tracks. In addition, the construction to rebuild and enlarge the station building was completed, and it was reborn as "JR Hakata City", the largest station building in Japan.
章节.Station name signs:
On the Sanyo Shinkansen, from the opening until the late JNR era, station name signs of a unique style used only on this line were employed. This style, while similar to the station name signs of conventional lines of the time, omitted all hiragana notation. That is, the station name signs at the opening of the Tokaido Shinkansen (which in their case showed only the station's kanji plus romanization; however, these too were exchanged for JNR-standard station name signs in the mid-1970s) only added the names of the previous and next stations, likewise in kanji plus romanization.

However, this unique style of station name sign was not adopted on the Shinkansen from the Tohoku and Joetsu Shinkansen onward, and on the Sanyo Shinkansen as well, from the late JNR era the signs were successively exchanged for JNR-standard ones, the same signs as those adopted from the Tohoku and Joetsu Shinkansen onward with a specification almost identical to that of conventional lines, and the kanji plus romanization style of station name sign disappeared around the time of the privatization and division. The JNR-standard station name signs they were replaced with were also replaced again from the first half of the 1990s onward, at all stations, with signs of the specification common to JR West (at Shin-Osaka Station only, of the JR Central specification), and because they were abolished after only a very short period, none of them survive today.
章节.Overview and transition of rolling stock:
The transition of rolling stock operated on the Sanyo Shinkansen is as follows.

During the JNR era until 1987 (Showa 62), there was a long period of operation with only the 0 series, and the number of cars per formation was also almost fixed at 16. After that, JNR was privatized and divided, with the Tokaido Shinkansen going to JR Central and the Sanyo Shinkansen to JR West, and vehicle development and formations unique to the Sanyo Shinkansen unfolded. One aspect was higher speed, and the 500 series, which enabled high-speed operation at 300 km/h, is a representative example. In addition, formations specialized for transport demand were organized, and shortening of formations to four, six, and eight cars, not seen on the Tokaido Shinkansen, also advanced. Including through-service vehicles with the Tokaido Shinkansen, which absolutely required 16-car formations with 1,323 seats, a wide variety of types and formations came to be operated. Exceptionally, the 500 series differs in seat count and arrangement from the 300 series and vehicles after the 700 series, but through-service vehicles for the Tokaido Shinkansen from the 300 series onward, also because of their train assignments (so that the seats remain the same even when a substitute train is used), are designed in principle so that the seat count and arrangement remain constant up to the N700S.

In addition, since the 100 series and 300 series ended operation in the spring of 2012, all passenger vehicles running on the Sanyo Shinkansen have since been compatible with a maximum speed of 285 km/h or more.
章节.Outline of each type: The service vehicles on the Sanyo Shinkansen are outlined below. For details, refer to the article on each vehicle. In addition, all service vehicles have won either the Blue Ribbon Award or the Laurel Prize.
章节.0 series:
A vehicle introduced by JNR at the opening of the Tokaido Shinkansen in 1964 (Showa 39), with 3,216 cars manufactured over more than 20 years until 1986 (Showa 61). For this reason, there are various specifications depending on the year of manufacture. The maximum speed at appearance was 210 km/h. On November 1, 1986 (Showa 61), it was raised to 220 km/h to match the 100 series.

An all-motor system was adopted, and formations could be increased or decreased in two-car units. In addition to ordinary cars and Green cars, vehicles providing food service such as buffet and dining cars were incorporated, and production advanced with formations of 12 or 16 cars.

In addition, because of the increase in the number of tunnels, the number of times ventilation had to be cut off to counter changes in cabin air pressure increased, so a continuous ventilation system was adopted at stations west of Okayama, which opened later. For this reason, formations incorporating 0 series vehicles manufactured before 1973 (Showa 48) could not enter west of Okayama Station. In the S and Y formations of the Tokaido "Kodama", the formation numbers were set to the original formation number plus 50 to identify formations prohibited from entering west of Okayama.

On the Sanyo Shinkansen, where the transport scale is smaller than on the Tokaido Shinkansen, formations were also shortened in line with demand. In the late JNR era, in 1985 (Showa 60), six-car formations of ordinary cars only appeared for "Kodama" on the Sanyo Shinkansen. After JR West was established, "West Hikari" in six-, eight-, and 12-car formations appeared, with interior improvements such as four seats abreast in a row. In later years four-car formations were added, and until 2008 (Heisei 20) they were mainly used for "Kodama".
章节.100 series:
Introduced in 1985 (Showa 60) as the first model-change vehicle in Shinkansen history, with the aim of replacing the 0 series, which had been manufactured for a long time and had become obsolete. 1,056 cars were manufactured by JNR and, after privatization, by the newly established JR Central and JR West.

Although the service operation speed remained at 220 km/h, 10 km/h faster than before, by increasing motor output and adopting new brakes, four of the 16 cars in a formation were manufactured as trailers (vehicles without motors), reducing manufacturing costs. The interior was also improved in terms of accommodation, with the seat pitch expanded so that three-abreast seats could be rotated for the first time, and private compartments were also provided. In addition, a major feature was the inclusion of two double-deck vehicles, such as in the Green car and dining car. At JR West, the "Grand Hikari" formation (100N series), with four double-deck vehicles in the formation, was also manufactured, and the maximum speed was raised to 230 km/h. After the introduction of successor vehicles, it was shortened into formations like the 0 series, the double-deck vehicles were removed, and it came to be used only for "Kodama", ending service operation with the timetable revision of March 17, 2012 (Heisei 24).
章节.300 series:
A vehicle developed by JR Central with the aim of increasing the speed of the Tokaido Shinkansen. The maximum speed was raised to 270 km/h, and the "Nozomi" appeared along with this vehicle. Entry into the Sanyo Shinkansen began in 1993 (Heisei 5), connecting Shin-Osaka and Hakata in 2 hours 32 minutes, 17 minutes faster than before. In addition to JR Central, it was also manufactured by JR West, and by 1998 (Heisei 10) its total number reached 1,120 cars.

The body adopted an aluminum alloy instead of the previous steel, and resin components were actively used in the interior as well, with thorough weight reduction. In addition, AC motors with inverter control were adopted, achieving smaller size and higher output compared with conventional DC motors. On the other hand, dining cars, whose use had continued to decline, and double-deck vehicles, which hindered weight reduction and lowering of the center of gravity, were not incorporated, and the formation consisted of 16 cars of ordinary and Green cars only.

Although the 300 series achieved a major reduction in journey time through the increased maximum speed, from around this time the development and introduction of new types came one after another, and it began to have its scope of operation narrowed within just a few years of its appearance. In 2001 (Heisei 13) it left regular "Nozomi" operation, and on the Sanyo Shinkansen it was mainly used for Tokyo-through "Hikari" services east of Okayama. Furthermore, scrapping progressed from 2007 with the start of mass production of the N700 series, and operation ended with the timetable revision of March 17, 2012 (Heisei 24). In addition, this type was not shortened into formations like other series, and was the only type to retire from the Sanyo Shinkansen at the same time as from the Tokaido Shinkansen.
章节.500 series:
A vehicle developed by JR West with the aim of further increasing the speed of the Sanyo Shinkansen, achieving the first 300 km/h operation in Shinkansen history. Operation began in March 1997 (Heisei 9) as the "Nozomi" between Shin-Osaka Station and Hakata Station, shortening the journey time between Shin-Osaka and Hakata to 2 hours 17 minutes, 15 minutes faster than the 300 series.

To realize high-speed operation at 300 km/h, an all-motor formation with increased output was adopted for the first time since the 0 series. To reduce air resistance and noise, and to counter the thunderous noise in tunnels (tunnel micro-pressure waves) that occurs with high-speed operation, the body was made a rounded cross-section with the corners dropped and the cross-sectional area reduced, and the leading car is characterized by a 15 m long nose with a canopy-type cab, giving it an exterior different from other Shinkansen vehicles. Nine 16-car formations, 144 cars in all, were manufactured.

As the fastest vehicle on the Sanyo Shinkansen it was mainly used for "Nozomi" services, but because its capacity and seat arrangement differed from the 300 and 700 series, both also 16-car formations, and because of the operational problem that the leading car had only one door, from 2007 (Heisei 19) it gradually handed over its operations to the successor N700 series N formation owned by JR West, which appeared in July of that year, and left "Nozomi" operations in 2010 (Heisei 22). The surplus formations were reduced to eight cars (at the same time, the Green cars were converted to ordinary reserved-seat cars), with the maximum speed lowered to 285 km/h, and from 2008 (Heisei 20) they began operation on "Kodama" services in place of the 0 series six-car formations.
章节.700 series:
A vehicle that began service operation in 1999 (Heisei 11), jointly developed by JR Central and JR West. It was manufactured with the aim of replacing the 0 and 100 series, which had low maximum speeds.

The 500 series made 300 km/h operation possible on the Sanyo Shinkansen, but it had major problems, such as high manufacturing costs and constraints on cabin space due to the emphasis on aerodynamic performance. In addition, on the Tokaido Shinkansen, with inferior alignment conditions, it was limited to 270 km/h, equivalent to the 300 series, and could not demonstrate performance commensurate with its cost. Therefore, the 700 series emphasized cost-effectiveness, aiming to raise the overall level of the entire Tokaido-Sanyo Shinkansen, with the main focus on improving ride comfort. The maximum speed was set slightly lower than the 500 series, at 285 km/h, and a unique nose shape resembling a platypus was adopted. This shape was intended to suppress tunnel micro-pressure waves while minimizing the effect on cabin space.

1,200 cars were manufactured by JR Central and JR West together for 16-car "Nozomi" formations, and in addition, at JR West, 128 cars were manufactured as eight-car formations for the "Hikari Rail Star", operated only on the Sanyo Shinkansen, as the successor to the "West Hikari". The former left regular "Nozomi" operations on the Sanyo Shinkansen with the March 12, 2011 revision as N700 series production increased, and was used for extra "Nozomi" services and regular "Hikari" and "Kodama" services. After that, regular operation within the Sanyo Shinkansen ended on March 13, 2020 (Reiwa 2), after which one B4 formation remained as an extra-service vehicle, but it was scrapped as of February 28, 2021 (Reiwa 3).

The E formations for the "Hikari Rail Star" consist of ordinary cars only, and a unique color scheme is adopted for the livery. Car 8 has an ordinary compartment. With the start of through operation with the Kyushu Shinkansen, many were replaced by through-service "Sakura" trains, and they are now mainly used for "Kodama" services in place of the 100 series, but they are also allocated to extra "Nozomi" services that run entirely within the Sanyo Shinkansen.
章节.N700 series:
A vehicle based on the 700 series, with the keywords "fastest, comfortable, and environmentally friendly", aiming at further performance improvement. Jointly developed by JR Central and JR West, service operation began in 2007 (Heisei 19).

Weight reduction, improved aerodynamic performance, and increased motor output made 300 km/h operation on the Sanyo Shinkansen possible for the first time since the 500 series. Although the maximum speed on the Tokaido Shinkansen remains 270 km/h as before, the reduction in the number of decelerations through improved acceleration performance and the introduction of the first body-tilting system in Shinkansen history achieved shorter journey times. The exterior follows the 700 series, but is characterized by the nose shape called the Aero Double-Wing, full circumferential skirts on the connections to reduce air resistance, somewhat small windows, and large full-color LED destination displays. In addition, all seats in the interior were made non-smoking, with separate smoking rooms provided.

As replacements for the 500 and 700 series, they continued to be introduced on "Nozomi" services, reaching a total of about 1,500 cars by 2011 (Heisei 23).

Of those operated on the Sanyo Shinkansen, there are two types: the X and K formations (2000 and 5000 subseries), 16-car formations converted from 2013 (Heisei 25) with the introduction of the N700A described below, and the S and R formations (7000 and 8000 subseries), eight-car formations for Kyushu Shinkansen through services that began service operation in March 2011 (Heisei 23). With the introduction of the N700S described below, replacement of the X formations owned by JR Central began from 2020 (Reiwa 2).
章节.N700A:
In May 2011 (Heisei 23), JR Central announced the introduction of the "N700A" ("A" is the initial letter of Advanced), an improved version of the N700 series. Operation began from 2013 (Heisei 25).

Numerous improvements were made from the perspectives of ensuring safety and punctuality and of environmental performance and ride comfort, such as improvements to the brakes, body-tilting system, and passenger-service equipment, and the new installation of a constant-speed running device.

G and F formations (1000 and 4000 subseries), 16-car formations, are operated.
章节.N700S:
On June 24, 2016 (Heisei 28), JR Central announced the introduction of the "N700S" ("S" is an abbreviation of Supreme, meaning "the best"). Power outlets are installed at all 1,323 passenger seats, and safety measures have been enhanced, such as a 5% shorter stopping distance when an earthquake occurs, the ability for the integrated control center to also view images from in-car security cameras in emergencies, and the installation of the first battery self-propulsion system in Shinkansen history, enabling the train to run under its own power to a place where evacuation is easy even during long power outages caused by natural disasters. In addition, the nose shape has been improved to reduce air resistance and noise when entering tunnels, contributing to a 15-ton reduction in total formation weight and a 7% reduction in power consumption compared with the N700A series. A test vehicle appeared in March 2018 (Heisei 30), and service operation began on July 1, 2020 (Reiwa 2).

J and H formations (0 and 3000 subseries), 16-car formations, are operated.

章节.In-car chimes and announcements:
From November 24, 2003 (Heisei 15), the music of the chimes used for in-car announcements on vehicles belonging to JR West has been "Ii Hi Tabidachi - Nishi e" ("Good Day for a Journey - Westward"), a 2003 cover by Chihiro Onitsuka of "Ii Hi Tabidachi", once sung by Shinji Tanimura and Momoe Yamaguchi. In addition, on vehicles belonging to JR Central, "Ai ni Iko" by UA is used, and on vehicles belonging to JR Kyushu, the original composition "The Journey" by Minoru Mukamiya is used (except when arriving at and departing from Hakata Station).

Until March 11, 2011, only car 4 of the Hikari Rail Star was set as a "silence car", in which no in-car announcements were made except before departure from the first station, just before arrival at the last station, and in emergencies.

From June 20, 2008 (Heisei 20), the in-car chime of the 0 series was returned to the "old Kodama / old Hikari" chime used until 2003 (Heisei 15), and it was used until November 30 of that year, when the series ended regular operation.

In the "500 TYPE EVA", which used 500 series V2 formations and was operated from November 2015 to May 2018, "A Cruel Angel's Thesis", the theme song of the television anime "Neon Genesis Evangelion", was used.
章节.Train names: For details such as stopping stations east of Shin-Osaka Station and south of Hakata Station, refer to the articles on each train, and to "Tokaido Shinkansen" and "Kyushu Shinkansen".
章节.\"Nozomi\":
The "Nozomi" is the fastest type of train, newly established on the Sanyo Shinkansen on March 18, 1993 (Heisei 5). Initially, it was operated at a rate of about one to two trains per hour. After the timetable revision of October 1, 2003 (Heisei 15), it was positioned as the mainstay train of the Tokaido-Sanyo Shinkansen in place of the "Hikari", and its frequency was greatly increased. The train-type color shown on the destination sign is yellow.

Within the Sanyo Shinkansen, all trains stop at Shin-Osaka Station, Shin-Kobe Station, Okayama Station, Hiroshima Station, Kokura Station, and Hakata Station, while one train per hour each stops selectively at the three stations of Himeji Station, Fukuyama Station, and Shin-Yamaguchi Station, four round trips per day at Tokuyama Station, and one train each way at Nishi-Akashi Station. In principle, selective stopping within the Sanyo Shinkansen is at one of four stations, and trains stopping at two or more stations are designated "Sakura" or "Hikari", but in the early morning up direction and at night in the down direction, "Nozomi" trains with two selective stops, on the same footing as "Sakura" and "Hikari", are also scheduled. Conversely, there is also one up train that makes no selective stop. Initially, Okayama Station, Hiroshima Station, and Kokura Station were served by all trains, and Shin-Kobe Station by some trains. With the timetable revision of October 1, 2003 (Heisei 15), all Nozomi trains came to stop at Shin-Kobe Station, and many "Hikari" services between Tokyo Station and Hiroshima Station/Hakata Station were changed to "Nozomi", and at the same time Himeji Station, Fukuyama Station, Tokuyama Station, and Shin-Yamaguchi Station were added as stopping stations. With the timetable revision of March 15, 2008 (Heisei 20), one train departing Nishi-Akashi for Tokyo was scheduled.

Under the timetable as of June 20, 2015, three trains per hour were operated: two regular trains between Tokyo Station and Hakata Station and one regular train between Tokyo Station and Hiroshima Station. However, because Shinkansen trains cannot operate between 0:00 and 6:00, morning and night trains are operated over shorter sections than this. At one time, "Nozomi" trains only within the Sanyo Shinkansen (between Shin-Osaka Station and Hakata Station) were also operated in the morning and at night, but these were replaced by the "Mizuho", whose operation began on March 12, 2011. Since then, all regular trains run through to the Tokaido Shinkansen.

All are operated with N700 series trains (16-car formations, 1,323 seats). In addition, until March 2012 the 300 series was used, until the end of February 2010 the 500 series, and until the end of February 2020 the 700 series. When the timetable is disrupted and extra "Nozomi" trains ending entirely within the Sanyo Shinkansen are operated, 700 series 7000 subseries for the "Hikari Rail Star" or N700 series 7000/8000 subseries for "Mizuho" and "Sakura" may also be allocated.
章节.\"Mizuho\":
The "Mizuho" is the fastest type of train, operating through between Shin-Osaka Station and Kagoshima-Chuo Station on the Sanyo and Kyushu Shinkansen. Operation began simultaneously with the full-line opening of the Kyushu Shinkansen (Kagoshima route) on March 12, 2011 (Heisei 23). It is now operated eight round trips per day, mainly in the morning and evening. The train-type color is orange.

Within the Sanyo Shinkansen it is positioned as the same fastest type of train as the "Nozomi", and its fare system is also based on that of the "Nozomi". All trains stop at Shin-Osaka Station, Shin-Kobe Station, Okayama Station, Hiroshima Station, Kokura Station, and Hakata Station within the Sanyo Shinkansen, and some trains also stop at Himeji Station, Fukuyama Station, and Shin-Yamaguchi Station. There are no scheduled trains stopping at Tokuyama Station, where some "Nozomi" trains stop. All "Mizuho" trains run through to the Kyushu Shinkansen.

All trains are operated with N700 series trains (eight-car formations).
章节.\"Sakura\":
The "Sakura" is a train operating through between Shin-Osaka Station and Kagoshima-Chuo Station on the Sanyo and Kyushu Shinkansen. On the Sanyo Shinkansen, it plays the role of a semi-express type train. The train-type color is pink.

Operation began simultaneously with the full-line opening of the Kyushu Shinkansen (Kagoshima route) on March 12, 2011 (Heisei 23). The "Sakura" plays the role of a train operating through the Sanyo and Kyushu Shinkansen, and because operation began in a form integrating the "Hikari Rail Star", its stopping stations within the Sanyo Shinkansen follow the conventional stopping pattern of the "Hikari Rail Star".

Within the Sanyo Shinkansen, all trains stop at Shin-Osaka Station, Shin-Kobe Station, Okayama Station, Fukuyama Station, Hiroshima Station, Kokura Station, and Hakata Station, and stop at one or two of Nishi-Akashi Station, Himeji Station, Tokuyama Station, Shin-Yamaguchi Station, and Shin-Shimonoseki Station. As of March 18, 2023, 16 round trips are operated between Shin-Osaka Station and Kagoshima-Chuo Station, one round trip between Shin-Osaka Station and Kumamoto Station, and one round trip between Hiroshima Station and Kagoshima-Chuo Station, and in the down direction only there is one train from Shin-Shimonoseki to Kagoshima-Chuo. Like the "Mizuho", all "Sakura" trains run through to the Kyushu Shinkansen.

All "Sakura" trains operated on the Sanyo Shinkansen are operated with N700 series trains (eight-car formations).
章节.\"Hikari\":
The "Hikari" is a semi-express type of train (partly an all-stations type) that has existed since the opening of the Tokaido Shinkansen. The train-type color shown on the destination sign is red.

Initially, except for some in the morning and evening, almost all trains ran through to the Tokaido Shinkansen. After the privatization and division of JNR, operation of the "West Hikari", arriving at and departing from points within the Sanyo Shinkansen, also began, and this later shifted to the "Hikari Rail Star".

The "Hikari" on the Sanyo Shinkansen was once operated in various forms, as a "semi-express train", a "train passing some stations", and an "all-stations train", and was operated for a long time from the opening of the Sanyo Shinkansen as the mainstay semi-express train of the Tokaido-Sanyo Shinkansen. After the timetable revision of October 1, 2003 (Heisei 15), in which the fastest type, the "Nozomi", was greatly increased, the role of semi-express trains running through to the Tokaido Shinkansen shifted to the "Nozomi". With the start of operation of the "Sakura", running through to the Kyushu Shinkansen, on March 12, 2011 (Heisei 23), semi-express trains ending within the Sanyo Shinkansen were integrated into the "Sakura", and they are now operated as trains complementing the "Nozomi", "Mizuho", and "Sakura".

The Tokaido Shinkansen through system, except for some trains, stops at all stations within the Sanyo Shinkansen, and is operated mainly as a train complementing the "Kodama" between Shin-Osaka Station and Okayama Station. In past timetables, there were trains departing Mihara for Tokyo early in the morning and trains departing Tokyo for Himeji at night. All of these stopped at all stations within the Sanyo Shinkansen. In addition, the Mihara departure appeared with the timetable revision of March 15, 2008 (Heisei 20), and was one of the few "Hikari" trains stopping at Shin-Onomichi Station and Shin-Kurashiki Station, but with the timetable revision of March 2012 its first station became Hiroshima Station. In addition, in the morning down direction only, one train each from Shin-Yokohama to Hiroshima, from Nagoya to Hiroshima, and from Nagoya to Hakata is scheduled, and these stop at each of Shin-Kobe Station, Himeji Station, Okayama Station, and Fukuyama Station within the Sanyo Shinkansen, and at one or two of Nishi-Akashi Station, Aioi Station, and Shin-Shimonoseki Station.

In addition, "Hikari" trains ending entirely within the Sanyo Shinkansen are also operated, and of these, trains using 700 series 7000 subseries (eight-car E formations) are operated under the nickname "Hikari Rail Star". The "Hikari Rail Star" began operation in March 2000 (Heisei 12), taking over from the "West Hikari", which had begun operation after the privatization and division of JNR.

Trains running through to the Tokaido Shinkansen use N700 series trains (16-car formations). In the past, the 0, 100, and 300 series and the 700 series (16-car formations) were also used. Of the trains ending within the Sanyo Shinkansen, three trains: two use N700 series (16-car formations) and one uses the 700 series (eight-car formation) "Hikari Rail Star".

At one time at least a few "Hikari" trains stopped at every station on the Sanyo Shinkansen, but with the timetable revision of November 29, 1997 (Heisei 9), the stopping stations were reorganized and some stations were removed from the stopping stations. For "Hikari" trains running through to the Tokaido Shinkansen, after the timetable revision of October 1, 2003 (Heisei 15), no trains corresponding to "semi-express trains" were operated, and in the daytime only one "Hikari" per hour (stopping at all stations within the Sanyo Shinkansen) between Tokyo Station and Okayama Station came to be operated. Between Hiroshima Station and Hakata Station, with this revision there were no more "Hikari" trains running through from Tokyo, and because the "Hikari" operated between Nagoya Station and Hakata Station was changed to arriving at and departing from Hiroshima Station with the timetable revision of March 14, 2009 (Heisei 21), all service came to be operated by "Hikari Rail Star" arriving at and departing from Shin-Osaka Station.

Many of the "Hikari Rail Star" services arriving at and departing from points within the Sanyo Shinkansen were also reduced in a form replaced by the "Sakura", with the start of operation of the "Sakura" on March 12, 2011 (Heisei 23). After that, as production of the N700 series 7000 subseries (eight-car S formations) advanced, the 700 series 7000 subseries "Hikari Rail Star" was successively replaced by N700 series 7000 subseries "Hikari" trains. With the timetable revision of March 17, 2012 (Heisei 24), due to the further increase in "Sakura" services accompanying the completion of N700 series 7000 subseries production, regular "Hikari Rail Star" services were reduced to only one morning up train from Hakata to Shin-Osaka, and even all "Hikari" services arriving at and departing from points within the Sanyo Shinkansen were reduced to two round trips. Although regular "Hikari Rail Star" services were increased to one down and two up trains with the March 16, 2013 (Heisei 25) revision, with the timetable revision of March 12, 2022 (Reiwa 4), the down train from Shin-Osaka to Hakata was abolished, leaving only two up trains, from Kokura to Okayama and from Hakata to Shin-Osaka, and with the timetable revision of March 18, 2023 (Reiwa 5), only one up train, from Shin-Shimonoseki to Okayama, remained.
章节.\"Kodama\":
The "Kodama" is an all-stations type train that has existed since the opening of the Tokaido Shinkansen, and stops at all stations. The train-type color shown on the destination sign is originally blue, but on the in-car electronic display boards of 500 and 700 series vehicles, green is used because of the light-emission characteristics.

Due to the increase and acceleration of semi-express trains, there is much waiting at stopping stations for trains to pass, and journey times have become longer; as of the March 2015 timetable revision, they are 4 hours 10 minutes to 5 hours 20 minutes between Shin-Osaka Station and Hakata Station. "Kodama" trains departing Hakata between 10:00 and 14:00 for Shin-Osaka all stop at Okayama Station for 24 to 33 minutes, and the journey time to Shin-Osaka takes more than five hours, but at Okayama Station they connect with a "Hikari" starting at Okayama and stopping at all stations within the Sanyo Shinkansen, and by changing to this train one can travel the entire Sanyo Shinkansen in 4 hours 40 minutes on an all-stations basis (for reference, at the opening there were three fewer stations than now, and all trains traveled between Shin-Osaka Station and Hakata Station in about 4 hours 30 minutes). Since March 18, 2006 (Heisei 18), the number of trains has been reduced with each timetable revision. In particular, between Shin-Osaka Station and Okayama Station there are time periods with no daytime "Kodama" services, and the aforementioned "Hikari" between Tokyo Station and Okayama Station plays the role of the "Kodama".

They are mainly operated with eight-car formations of the 700 and 500 series, and in early-morning and late-night trains, 16-car formations of the N700 series and eight-car formations of the N700 series are also used, though in very small numbers. In the past the 0, 100, and 300 series were also used, but operation with the 0 series, which had existed since the opening, ended on November 30, 2008 (Heisei 20). The 100 series also operated four-car trains on a limited basis between Hakata Station and Okayama Station, but operation of the four-car formations ended with the timetable revision of March 12, 2011, and operation of the six-car formations between Okayama Station and Shin-Osaka Station also ended with this revision, and by the timetable revision of March 17, 2012 all formations of the 100 series had ended operation together with the 300 series. As a result, all "Kodama" trains were unified into eight- and 16-car formations.

Between Kokura Station and Hakata Station, and on some trains in the morning and evening, all cars are non-reserved. Some trains operate through to the Hakata-Minami Line, treated as a conventional line, as limited express trains.
章节.\"Tsubame\": The "Tsubame" is a train operated stopping at all stations within the Kyushu Shinkansen (equivalent to the "Kodama" on the Sanyo Shinkansen), but with the timetable revision of March 17, 2012 (Heisei 24), two up trains (one from Kumamoto to Shin-Shimonoseki and one from Kagoshima-Chuo to Kokura) entered the Sanyo Shinkansen. They were also operated stopping at all stations within the Sanyo Shinkansen, and all vehicles used were N700 series eight-car formations. With the timetable revision of March 16, 2013 (Heisei 25), they were reorganized to arrive at and depart from points within the Kyushu section, and regular trains no longer entered the Sanyo section, but from March 4, 2017, one train, Tsubame 306 from Kumamoto to Kokura, was scheduled, and although within Kyushu island, through operation was restored. The train-type color is light blue.

章节.Transition of journey times:
The transition of journey times for the fastest trains between Shin-Osaka Station and Hakata Station is shown below.
March 10, 1975 (Showa 50) - 3 hours 44 minutes, "Hikari", 0 series
The Sanyo Shinkansen fully opened. The maximum speed was 210 km/h. The stations served by the fastest train (W Hikari) were Okayama, Hiroshima, and Kokura.
October 1, 1980 (Showa 55) - 3 hours 28 minutes, "Hikari", 0 series
Speed restrictions between Mihara Station and Hakata Station, which had been in place because the ground had not settled, were lifted, and speeds increased.
March 14, 1985 (Showa 60) - 3 hours 16 minutes, "Hikari", 0 series
The margin times were reviewed, and speeds increased.
November 1, 1986 (Showa 61) - 2 hours 59 minutes, "Hikari", 0 and 100 series
The maximum speed was raised from 210 km/h to 220 km/h.
March 11, 1989 (Heisei 1) - 2 hours 49 minutes, "Hikari", 100 series V formation (100N series)
The 100 series "Grand Hikari" began operating, and the maximum speed became 230 km/h.
March 18, 1993 (Heisei 5) - 2 hours 32 minutes, "Nozomi", 300 series
The 300 series "Nozomi" began operating on the Sanyo Shinkansen as well. The maximum speed was 270 km/h.
March 22, 1997 (Heisei 9) - 2 hours 17 minutes, "Nozomi", 500 series
The 500 series "Nozomi" began operating. The maximum speed was 300 km/h, then the fastest in the world. In addition, the 700 series "Nozomi", which began operating on March 13, 1999 (Heisei 11), took 2 hours 25 minutes (now 2 hours 28 minutes, maximum speed 285 km/h), and the 700 series 7000 subseries "Hikari Rail Star", which began operating from March 11, 2000 (Heisei 12), took 2 hours 45 minutes (before the opening of the Kyushu Shinkansen, the semi-express type was a standard 2 hours 40 minutes, maximum speed 285 km/h).
October 1, 2003 (Heisei 15) - 2 hours 21 minutes, "Nozomi", 500 series
All trains, including the 500 series "Nozomi", came to stop at Shin-Kobe Station, lengthening the journey by four minutes.
March 18, 2006 (Heisei 18) - 2 hours 23 minutes, "Nozomi", 500 series (from July 1, 2007 also the N700 series)
Affected by the JR Fukuchiyama Line derailment accident, a "relaxed timetable" was implemented on the Sanyo Shinkansen as well, lengthening the journey by two minutes. From July 1, 2007 (Heisei 19), the N700 series began operating, with the same maximum speed of 300 km/h as the 500 series, taking 2 hours 23 minutes.
March 12, 2011 (Heisei 23) - 2 hours 22 minutes, "Nozomi", N700 series
Because the departure time of "Nozomi" 66, which had operated between Hakata Station and Shin-Osaka Station in 2 hours 23 minutes and between Hakata Station and Tokyo Station in 4 hours 51 minutes (Hakata 18:54 dep.-Shin-Osaka 21:17 arr., 20 dep.-Tokyo 23:45 arr.), was changed from Hakata Station at 18:55 to 18:55, a train running between Hakata Station and Shin-Osaka Station in 2 hours 22 minutes appeared. This was the first shortening of journey time since the implementation of the "relaxed timetable". In addition, the shortest journey time of the "Mizuho", whose operation began the same day, between Shin-Osaka Station and Hakata Station was 2 hours 23 minutes, the same as the conventional "Nozomi".
March 4, 2017 (Heisei 29) - 2 hours 21 minutes, "Nozomi", N700 series
As in 2011, the departure time of the last "Nozomi" 64 between Hakata Station and Tokyo Station was delayed by one minute, so it ran between Hakata Station and Shin-Osaka Station in 2 hours 21 minutes, returning to the journey time before the "relaxed timetable" was implemented. (Hakata 18:59 dep.-Shin-Osaka 21:20 arr., 21:23 dep.-Tokyo 23:45 arr.)
In addition, the fastest timetable of the "Mizuho" is 2 hours 22 minutes up and 2 hours 23 minutes down. The journey time of the fastest down "Nozomi" train is 2 hours 28 minutes.

章节.Keihanshin - Fukuoka:
Between Keihanshin and Fukuoka, the Sanyo Shinkansen competes with air services between Itami Airport/Kansai International Airport and Fukuoka Airport. Under the policy of the Ministry of Transport, the number of air services on this section was greatly restricted for a long period from the opening of the Shinkansen to Hakata in 1975 (Showa 50), in order to stimulate demand for the Sanyo Shinkansen.

After its establishment, JR West provided comfortable in-car services with the "West Hikari" with its 2+2 seating, while introducing the "Grand Hikari" and 300 series "Nozomi" and improving its speed-based express services. Even after the opening of Kansai International Airport in 1994 (Heisei 6), in 1997 (Heisei 9) it relaxed and abolished restrictions on the use of the Tokutoku Kippu within the Sanyo section (during ultra-peak periods such as the Bon holidays and New Year) and issued inexpensive coupon tickets, along with the introduction of the 500 series vehicle with a maximum speed of 300 km/h.

However, by that time, due to deregulation such as the abolition of the 45/47 system, the restrictions on the number of air services by the Ministry of Land, Infrastructure, Transport and Tourism had also been abolished, and the airlines adopted measures such as increasing air services from Osaka Airport to Kyushu and expanding mileage services, so the Shinkansen gradually lost share. Therefore, in 2000 (Heisei 12) JR West introduced the "Hikari Rail Star", and the high-quality service, such as its 2+2 reserved seating, became popular, and the Shinkansen's share began to increase. The decline in air demand continued, and the Shinkansen share is now at its highest ever.

On the other hand, the low-cost carrier (LCC) Peach Aviation has been intermittently serving routes between Kansai International Airport and various parts of Kyushu, including Fukuoka Airport, from March 2012 onward, and JR West president Takayuki Sasaki stated that "we cannot compete (with LCCs) on fares alone", indicating an intention to compete through convenience, such as expanding the areas where mobile phones can be used on board. In fiscal 2012, share fell slightly due to the LCC effect, and in 2013 the Super Hayatoku Ticket (between Shin-Osaka/Shin-Kobe and Kokura/Hakata: 10,000 yen; departures from Kumamoto and Kagoshima-Chuo are also offered), which can be used cheaply even during peak periods, albeit only through the internet reservation service e5489, went on sale.

章节.Within Fukuoka Prefecture:
Between Kokura and Hakata, use as a means of commuting increased rapidly from the launch of sales of Shinkansen commuter passes (FREX) on January 31, 1983, and the number of users of the single Shinkansen station-to-station section reached 7,900 per day, the highest in the country. In response, from July 1, 1983, shuttle-operation "Kodama" services between Kokura and Hakata were scheduled (initially as daily extra trains), and even after becoming regular trains they were strengthened with timetable revisions such as those of June 24, 1985 and March 22, 1997. This Kodama was initially operated by making use of the gaps between vehicle runs, but from June 24, 1985, newly built 0 series R0 formations with stickers indicating Kokura-Hakata, as vehicles dedicated to this section, began operation limited to this section. In the down direction on this section, from June 20, 1983, a special arrangement was introduced allowing passengers with tickets valid in non-reserved cars to sit in empty reserved seats to relieve congestion, but this arrangement was abolished as of March 11, 2011, due to the start of through operation with the Kyushu Shinkansen.

In addition, the number of shuttle-operation "Kodama" services between Kokura and Hakata has been on a declining trend, partly due to the increase in "Nozomi" services arriving at and departing from Hakata to two per hour in March 2006.

章节.Fares and limited express charges:
Fares are calculated based on operating kilometers. The operating kilometers between Shin-Osaka Station and Hakata Station are the same as those of the parallel Tokaido Main Line (Shin-Osaka-Kobe), Sanyo Main Line (Kobe-Moji), and Kagoshima Main Line (Moji-Hakata). The Shin-Iwakuni Station-Tokuyama Station section is designated as a route-specific section, and like the parallel Sanyo Main Line it uses the fare-calculating kilometers via the Gantetsu Line (the difference between operating kilometers and fare-calculating kilometers is 4.4 km).

Limited express charges are set individually for each station pair by what is called a "triangular table". On the other hand, these limited express charges for each station pair are calculated based on the operating kilometers of the section concerned. The limited express charges corresponding to operating kilometers, and those for other specific sections, are as shown in the separate table.

The table on the right shows the limited express charges when using only the Sanyo Shinkansen, or when using it across both the Sanyo Shinkansen and the Tokaido Shinkansen. For limited express charges when using only the Tokaido Shinkansen, see "Limited express charges on the Tokaido Shinkansen".
When using the Sanyo Shinkansen and the Kyushu Shinkansen, the limited express charges are not totaled, and the individual charges up to Hakata Station are added together. For limited express charges on the Kyushu Shinkansen, see "Limited express charges on the Kyushu Shinkansen".
Reserved-seat limited express charges are uniformly 200 yen cheaper in off-peak periods and uniformly 200 yen more expensive in peak periods (uniformly 400 yen more expensive in the new maximum-peak period to be introduced from April 2023). Non-reserved seats are the same price throughout the year. With Express Reservation, reserved seats are also the same price throughout the year.
When using a Green car, the amount is the limited express charge of the same amount as the non-reserved limited express charge (but 1,760 yen for specific limited express ticket sections as well) plus the Green charge according to the section used (from the April 2023 boarding period, uniformly 200 yen cheaper in off-peak periods, uniformly 200 yen more expensive in peak periods, and uniformly 400 yen more expensive in maximum-peak periods, relative to the limited express charge portion (or the total amount)). See "Green charges".
The limited express charge when using a reserved seat on the "Nozomi" or "Mizuho" is the amount in the table on the right plus the surcharge for the section using a reserved seat on the "Nozomi" or "Mizuho" (the same as the amount in the table on the right when using a non-reserved seat). In addition, when using the "Mizuho" across both the Sanyo Shinkansen and the Kyushu Shinkansen, the surcharge applies only to the section between Hakata Station and Shin-Osaka Station, and no surcharge accrues within the Kyushu Shinkansen. See "Nozomi limited express charges".
章节.Special tickets:
On the Sanyo Shinkansen, discount tickets (special tickets) are set mainly for sections competing with highway buses and airlines, and sections with parallel lines of other companies.

Sanyo Shinkansen 2-Kippu (two-ticket set)
A two-ticket set discount ticket usable within Osaka City and Kobe City, and within Kitakyushu and Fukuoka cities.
It was sold from March 2006 (Heisei 18) as a replacement for the "Shinkansen Quartet Ticket" (a book of four tickets) abolished in May 2006 (Heisei 18), but was abolished as of November 30, 2011 (Heisei 23), on the grounds of the expanded use of Express Reservation.

Shinkansen Yoka Yoka Kippu
A round-trip discount ticket limited to Saturdays and holidays, set between Asa, Shin-Shimonoseki, and Kokura and Hakata. Valid for one day. Only round trips to Kokura Station are set for departures from Hakata.
It must be purchased either at a Midori no Madoguchi ticket machine near the departure or arrival station by the previous day, or reserved via e5489 by the previous day and the ticket collected at a Midori no Madoguchi ticket machine or a collection machine before boarding (also possible on the day).
In the past, it was also handled at JR West station windows, JR Kyushu windows, and major travel agencies around the departure point.

Shinkansen Round-Trip Discount Ticket
A discount ticket equivalent to JR Kyushu's planned ticket "2-Kippu", set for sections including the Sanyo Shinkansen Kokura-Hakata section. Sold jointly with JR Kyushu.
It is broadly divided into the following two types, and the former cannot use the Kyushu Shinkansen. In addition, neither type can travel between Kokura and Hakata on the conventional line.
Type transferring between the Sanyo Shinkansen non-reserved seat and JR Kyushu conventional limited express: "Within Kitakyushu City - Saga / Nagasaki / Sasebo" and "Within Fukuoka City - Beppu and Oita / Miyazaki and Miyakonojo"
Type allowing use of ordinary non-reserved seats on the Sanyo and Kyushu Shinkansen: "Within Kitakyushu City - Kumamoto and Suizenji / Kagoshima-Chuo"
章节.Collaborative services with JR Central:
From December 2005 (Heisei 17), the sections eligible for the discounted limited express tickets (e-tickets) on the Tokaido Shinkansen through the "Express Reservation" using the JR Central Express Card were expanded to Shin-Kobe Station, and JR West also newly issued the J-WEST Card, which allows the same service, from February 2006 (Heisei 18) (only the paid-annual-fee "Express" plan allows use of this service), and from July 22 of the same year service began on the entire Sanyo Shinkansen, while both cards became usable across the entire Tokaido-Sanyo Shinkansen. In addition, from August 29, 2009 (Heisei 21), the IC card system "EX-IC service" was expanded to the Sanyo section (it was introduced at the conventional line connecting ticket gates of both Kokura and Hakata stations on March 12, 2012), and in 2022 (Reiwa 4) it was expanded to the Kyushu Shinkansen section as well.

In addition, the "Mizuho", "Sakura", and "Tsubame" running through between the Kyushu Shinkansen and the Sanyo Shinkansen were also ineligible for Express Reservation and the EX-IC service in the Sanyo Shinkansen section (Shin-Osaka-Hakata), but from 5:30 a.m. on July 21, 2012, handling of Express Reservation in the Sanyo Shinkansen section began. However, use including the Kyushu Shinkansen section (Hakata Station-Kagoshima-Chuo Station), and the Green Program (an "upgrade" to the Green car with accumulated points) and early-discount services (such as EX-IC early-bird discounts) on the aforementioned three trains in the Sanyo Shinkansen section continue to be ineligible.
章节.(New) e5489:
From March 12, 2011, with the completion of the Kyushu Shinkansen (Kagoshima route) between Hakata Station and Kagoshima-Chuo Station, operation of the "Mizuho" and "Sakura", which run through with the Sanyo Shinkansen, began. These Sanyo-Kyushu Shinkansen through trains, and the "Sakura" and "Tsubame" operating within the Kyushu Shinkansen (some trains also enter the Sanyo Shinkansen section), can be purchased through an internet reservation service operated by JR West and JR Kyushu in cooperation.

From March 5, 2011, at JR West, the "(New) e5489" service was introduced in place of "e5489plus" (covering most JR West, JR Shikoku, and JR Kyushu trains, and some JR Central and JR East trains; for the JR Kyushu area, from March 12), and at JR Kyushu the functions of the "JR Kyushu Train Reservation Service" were enhanced correspondingly.

In particular, for J-WEST Card members, fares cheaper than usual ("(New) e-Ticket", equivalent to the conventional "e5489plus: e-wari Ticket") have been set. Unlike the conventional e-wari Ticket, this was changed to a service handling reservation and issuance of limited express tickets only, to be used in combination with ordinary tickets (until then, they had been sold as a set with a ticket for the same section as the limited express ticket, and if riding beyond the section covered by the e-wari Ticket, the ordinary fare for the excess section was separately required regardless of the passenger-kilometer band).

Furthermore, in the new service, although limited by section, train, equipment, and number of seats, the "e-Hayatoku", which is cheaper than the "(New) e-Ticket" with reservations up to three days before the boarding date, has also been set. This too is exclusive to J-WEST Card members and handles reservation and issuance of limited express tickets only, so it can be combined with ordinary tickets, round-trip discount tickets, and other discount tickets such as student discounts. On the Shinkansen it is set only between Shin-Osaka Station/Shin-Kobe Station and Kumamoto Station/Kagoshima-Chuo Station, but it is a highly convenient service on business trips and the like (it is also set as a Green car-only product on some JR West conventional limited expresses).

In addition, for JR Kyushu's JQ CARD members, the "(New) e-Ticket" and "e-Hayatoku" on the Sanyo-Kyushu Shinkansen can be purchased at the "JR Kyushu Train Reservation Service".
章节.Handling of the Shin-Shimonoseki - Hakat:
The Shin-Shimonoseki-Kokura-Hakata section is not treated as a separate line from the parallel conventional lines (Sanyo Main Line and Kagoshima Main Line), and its operating kilometers are set at the same distance as the conventional lines, but because the fare systems differ between JR West, which operates the Sanyo Shinkansen and the conventional lines between Shin-Shimonoseki and Shimonoseki, and JR Kyushu, which operates the conventional lines between Shimonoseki, Kokura, and Hakata, when traveling in this section it is necessary in advance to specify either "via the Shinkansen" or "via the conventional line", and it is not possible to board a conventional line with an ordinary ticket routed via the Shinkansen (or vice versa). In addition, because the sections that can be traveled with a Shinkansen commuter pass (FREX) are set as "ordinary non-reserved seats on the Shinkansen, and ordinary and rapid trains on the parallel conventional line", conventional lines can be traveled.

In addition, when using this section round trip, even if one way is via the Shinkansen and the other via the conventional line, it is sold as a "round-trip ticket", and if one way is 601 km or more, it is eligible for the round-trip discount (a 10% reduction in the fare for each of the outbound and return legs). The validity period is calculated as "the total of the outbound and return legs", unlike the handling of ordinary round-trip tickets (twice that of a one-way ticket).
章节.Safety of the Sanyo Shinkansen: At the time of construction, the country was in the midst of the period of high economic growth, and aggregate (sand) used as a concrete material was in short supply in the Chugoku, Shikoku, and Kyushu regions. For this reason, sea sand containing large amounts of salts, which corrode metals, was used. If sea sand is used as a concrete material, there is no problem provided the salts are washed out sufficiently. In practice, however, washing was not commonly carried out. In addition, strength tests after construction revealed that concrete below the design standard strength had been used. For this reason, it has been pointed out that concrete parts such as tunnels and piers deteriorate faster than in the Tokaido Shinkansen section. This is thought to be because the excessive salts and the highly air-permeable concrete are causing the reinforcing bars to rust severely (salt damage). In addition, an accident attributed to poor construction also occurred in 1999 (Heisei 11), when a falling piece of concrete struck a train in operation (the Fukuoka Tunnel concrete block falling accident). In connection with this, emergency inspections and repair work were carried out at various points on the line.
章节.History:
At the opening, the Sanyo Shinkansen did not operate "Kodama" services except during some time periods, and instead divided "Hikari" services into three types, operated respectively: the "W Hikari", stopping only at major stations within the Sanyo Shinkansen section; the "A Hikari", stopping at slightly more stations; and the "B Hikari", stopping at all stations, and almost all trains were operated through to Tokyo Station on the Tokaido Shinkansen.

However, because demand on the Sanyo Shinkansen was less than on the Tokaido Shinkansen, the number of trains was correspondingly small, and there were many time periods with only two round trips per hour, particularly west of Okayama. After that, beginning with the appearance of six-car-formation "Kodama" services running only within the Sanyo Shinkansen section in June 1985 (Showa 60), measures were adopted to shorten formations and increase the number of trains correspondingly.

With the privatization and division of JNR making it a JR West operating line, this trend gained further momentum, and many trains that were short-formed but improved in quality, such as the "West Hikari" and "Shuttle Hikari", with six to 12-car formations, came to be operated, and after the appearance of the eight-car-formation "Hikari Rail Star", "Kodama" services within the Sanyo section also became mostly four- to six-car formations (mostly mono-class cars with 2+2 seating using Green seats from scrapped vehicles), and this continues to the present.

In addition, because the Kokura-Hakata section competes with the parallel conventional Kagoshima Main Line, holders of regular tickets routed via the conventional line are permitted to travel on the Sanyo Shinkansen, and sectional trains on this section are scheduled mainly in the morning and evening time periods.

Regarding the "Hikari Rail Star", for a while after the appearance of the "Nozomi" on the Sanyo section, because the number of "Nozomi" trains themselves was small and their fares were relatively expensive, among other factors, the Shinkansen tended to be avoided, and it appeared as part of a countermeasure against air services; however, with the major increase in "Nozomi" services and the increase in stopping stations in the October 2003 (Heisei 15) timetable revision, along with a reduction in "Nozomi" fares (with regular non-reserved fares and discount tickets for sections such as between the Hanshin area and the Fukuoka area made the same for "Nozomi" use), the appearance of "Hikari Rail Star" semi-express trains of nearly "Nozomi" standard in the March 18, 2006 (Heisei 18) revision (now abolished), and the change of most "Hikari Rail Star" services to "Sakura" running through to the Kyushu Shinkansen with the revision accompanying the full-line opening of the Kyushu Shinkansen in 2011 (Heisei 23), its positioning is now somewhat ambiguous.

With the opening of the Kyushu Shinkansen between Hakata Station and Shin-Yatsushiro Station in March 2011 (Heisei 23), about one Sanyo-Kyushu through train per hour, the "Sakura" and "Mizuho", began operating. In addition, at Hakata Station, "Nozomi" trains arriving from Tokyo and "Sakura" trains turning back at Hakata allow transfers on the same platform.
